reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. Fetching the refunds table now.
The refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported exactly (orders 102, 103, 105 with the same amounts). Next I need the customer list, so I'll fetch the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly, so I can proceed. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 33983, which matches its orders (27247 + 18968) minus its refund on order 103 (12232). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net_cents is 65068, but its orders are 29562 + 35506 = 65068 with no refunds, which is consistent. Next I need cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net is 2634, which matches its orders (4653 + 33845 = 38498) minus refunds on orders 102 and 105 (2289 + 33575 = 35864). The refunds match Alpha's report and all three balances check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 33983 is recorded. Birch's balance of 65068 checks out against its unrefunded orders, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 2634 matches its orders minus the refunds on orders 102 and 105. Recording that payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, and each net balance matches orders minus refunds.
